intended_object: For two direct systems (F₁, f₁) and (F₂, f₂) over the same directed preorder, and a compatible family of maps ih_i : F₁ i → F₂ i (a morphism of direct systems, i.e. f₂ ∘ ih_i = ih_j ∘ f₁), this is the induced map lim F₁ → lim F₂ on the set-level direct limits, sending [i, x] to [i, ih_i x]. Inferred from the name, the body and `map_def`. The docstring is copied from `lift` and is slightly loose, but describes the same kind of construction.
explanation: The body applies `DirectLimit.lift` to the family x ↦ ⟦⟨i, ih i x⟩⟧ : F₁ i → DirectLimit F₂ f₂. The proof of well-definedness uses the compatibility condition and the directedness of ι. That `map_def` holds by `rfl` confirms it sends ⟦⟨i, x⟩⟧ to ⟦⟨i, ih i x⟩⟧, which is exactly the standard functorial map between colimits induced by a morphism of direct systems. It is stated in the natural generality for this file: any directed preorder, and any bundled function types with `FunLike`. Mathlib's other direct-limit maps, such as `Module.DirectLimit.map`, are algebraic versions of the same construction and are not more general. The docstring repeats the one for `lift`, so it describes defining a function out of the limit instead of the induced map, but this does not change the mathematical content. The definition is therefore faithful.
